name: NOTIFY
info:
CC NOTIFY — save the notification, then announce it.

Writes one row per recipient into `user_notifications`, THEN attempts the
web push. A failed / undelivered / never-subscribed push can no longer
lose a notification.

Replaces the old NOTIFY ADAPTER + PUSH NOTIFY pair. One node, not two.

=========================== RECIPIENTS ===========================
recipientMode:
  role -> notify role(s)      recipientValue = "billing,coordinator"
  user -> notify username(s)  recipientValue = "jsmith"
  all  -> everyone active     recipientValue ignored

recipientPath: msg path holding recipients resolved by your flow.
  Accepts an array or a comma-string. Dotted paths work.
  When set it OVERRIDES recipientValue. Resolves empty -> dropped.
  recipientMode still applies — it says which column to match against.

IMPORTANT: usernames, not display names.

============================ LEDGER ==============================
saveToInbox: yes (default) saves a user_notifications row per
  recipient and then pushes. No sends the push ONLY.

  Use "no" for snapshot-shaped notifications: a digest whose body is a
  count and a CTA ("5 orders overdue — tap to view") goes stale within
  hours, and a week of them crowds out the real events. Anything that
  states a fact about a record should stay on "yes".

  Skipping means a missed push is a lost notification, which is the
  failure this subflow exists to prevent. Treat it as the exception.

=========================== TEMPLATES ============================
dataRoot: where endpoint data lives (default: payload).
  {{field}} resolves relative to this.

tag: rendered per record. Give each notification a DISTINCT tag
  (include the record id) — Web Push collapses shared tags.

url: real deep link, and check the recipient's role can reach it.
  In the notification centre every entry is a permanent link, so
  ./home is a poor default and a page they can't open is worse.

===================== SETUP ON A NEW PROJECT =====================
See CC-NOTIFY-SETUP.md. In short:
  1. Run cc-notify.sql
  2. Point the web-push node at this project's VAPID config  <-- REQUIRED
  3. Check the three [3] resolve SELECTs match this project's user table
  4. Confirm the four DB nodes resolve (CopperCloud standard id)

l.en-US: no — push only, no inbox row

name: SETUP: point [10] push at this project's VAPID config
info:
The web-push node ships with NO vapidConfiguration. It will show a
red error on deploy until you pick one — that is deliberate. An
unset VAPID config is a silent no-send otherwise, and a red node
is a louder reminder than a line in a setup doc.

The four DB nodes reference the CopperCloud standard DB subflow
(cb85b1c398c1c3ab). If this project uses a different id, re-point
them — they will show as unknown-node otherwise.

The three [3] resolve SELECTs assume a `users` table with
`recid`, `username`, `userrole` (JSON) and `active`. Adjust them
here if this project's schema differs. Keep the `u` alias — the
role clause built in [1] depends on it.

info:
Role-Based Access Control middleware.

Wire AUTH_MIDDLEWARE output 3 → into this subflow.

Set ALLOWED_ROLES on each instance:
  admin                  → admin only
  admin,manager          → admin + manager
  admin,manager,operator → all roles

Outputs:
  1 → Authorised           → go to template / DB
  2 → Fetch denied (403)   → wire to http response
  3 → Browser denied (302) → wire to http response
